newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK FOREIGN MINISTER TO FLY TO ALBANIA.
newsitem.headline: GREEK FOREIGN MINISTER TO FLY TO ALBANIA.

text.p: Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis said on Wednesday he was sending his foreign minister to Albania to help defuse the violent crisis gripping its northern Balkan neighbour.
Theodoros Pangalos will fly to Tirana on Friday to meet Albanian President Sali Berisha, other government officials and opposition leaders, Simitis said in a live television interview.
"On Friday Mr Pangalos, escorted by (Deputy Foreign Minister Yannos) Kranidiotis will go to Tirana," he said.
Simitis said Kranidiotis would contact representatives of Albanian rebels controlling most southern towns and talk to them in an effort to end the conflict.

Greece, concerned with the crisis unfolding at its northern border, said earlier on Wednesday the rebels should be included in all-party talks in Tirana aimed at ending the violent uprising in the impoverished Balkan country.

The rebels have united under an umbrella group called the National Committee for People's Salvation, which called for Berisha's resignation and a separate seat at negotiations between Berisha and opposition parties.
Simitis said the only way to safeguard a large Greek minority in southern Albania, Greece and peace in the Balkans was for Albania to find a political solution and a path to democracy.
"The main thrust of our effort will be to make everyone communicate," Simitis said.
An armed uprising has swept southern Albania over the past two weeks, with dozens of towns and villages being taken over by rebels opposing Berisha.
The crisis was triggered when popular investment schemes collapsed in January, wiping out the savings of thousands of Albanians.
